english: The subject of the lesson was very interesting.
tip: X of Y takes two suffixes: -in on the owner, -i on the thing. Dersin konusu means the lesson's subject.

english: We couldn't go to the airport because of the rain.
tip: Yüzünden means because of and is used for unwanted causes. Yağmur yüzünden means because of the rain.

english: I haven't gotten my passport yet, I'm in the application process.
tip: Henüz plus a negative past verb means not yet. Henüz pasaportumu almadım means I haven't gotten my passport yet.

english: We walked through the field all the way to the forest.
tip: Kadar after a place in the dative means as far as. Ormana kadar means all the way to the forest.

target: Fırıncı her sabah taze ekmek pişirir.
english: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.
tip: The aorist -ir marks habits and general truths. Pişirir means bakes, as in bakes fresh bread every morning.

target: Küçük bir binanın üçüncü katında oturuyorum.
english: I live on the third floor of a small building.
tip: Ordinals add -üncü/-ıncı. Üç is three, üçüncü is third, as in üçüncü katında, on the third floor.

target: Ben bugün bulaşık yıkadım çünkü zamanım vardı.
english: I washed the dishes today because I had time.
tip: Çünkü (because) is unusual for Turkish: it sits before its reason clause. Çünkü zamanım vardı means because I had time.

target: Bu pasta çok hafif ve lezzetli, tarifi almalıyım.
english: This cake is very light and delicious, I must get the recipe.
tip: The suffix -malı/-meli means must or should. Al (get) plus -malıyım gives almalıyım, I must get.

english: Grapefruit is a slightly bitter fruit.
tip: The ending -dir gives a statement a general, factual tone. Meyvedir means is a fruit, stated as a plain fact.

english: Hasan bought the pastry from the bakery.
tip: The ablative -dan/-den means from. Fırın (bakery) plus -dan gives fırından, from the bakery.

english: I couldn't find it anywhere.
tip: bulamadım = bul (find) + ama (cannot) + dım (I did): I couldn't find. The -ama- slot marks inability, separate from plain negation.

english: My cousin got married last month.
tip: geçen means the one that passed, so geçen ay is last month and geçen hafta is last week. It sits before the time word.

english: I prepared very well for the exam.
tip: hazırlanmak (to prepare) attaches what you prepare for with dative -a, so you get ready Sınava, for the exam, not sınavı.

english: I learned to cook from my mother.
tip: yapmayı is yap (do) + ma (the act of) + yı (object mark): the cooking becomes the thing learned. Verbs turn into objects this way.

english: You can't go to the doctor without an appointment.
tip: almadan = al (take) + madan: without taking. Add -madan to a verb stem to say without doing that action.

english: I couldn't sleep all night because of the noise.
tip: Gürültüden uses ablative -den to give the cause: because of the noise. The -den ending can mean from or, as here, due to.

english: A good student studies regularly.
tip: öğrenci is öğren (learn) + ci: one who does it, a learner. The -ci ending names the person tied to the action or thing.

english: Dinner is very important during Ramadan.
tip: Ramazan'da takes an apostrophe before the suffix because Ramazan is a proper name: Ramazan + da becomes Ramazan'da.

english: I get up at seven every morning.
tip: Clock times take locative -de for at: yedide means at seven. So saat yedide is at seven o'clock.

english: A new hospital opened in our city.
tip: şehir drops its second vowel when a suffix follows, so şehir + imiz + de becomes Şehrimizde, in our city, not şehirimizde.

english: I prepared my suitcase before going on vacation.
tip: çıkmadan önce means before going. Use verb stem + madan önce for before doing something: çıkmadan önce, before leaving.

english: Egg with sucuk is a breakfast table favorite.
tip: Sucuklu is sucuk + lu: with sucuk. The -lu ending, also -lı, -li, -lü, means having or served with that thing.

english: Those who are curious ask, and those who ask learn.
tip: soran is sor (ask) + an: the one who asks. Add -an/-en to a verb to name the doer, like eden, the one who does.

english: I need to make a doctor's appointment next week.
tip: almam gerekiyor means I need to take. Build it as verb + ma + my + gerekiyor, so the necessity is personal: my taking is needed.

target: Dürüst insan her zaman saygı görür.
english: An honest person always gets respect.
tip: görmek here means to receive, not to see. saygı görür is gets respect, the same pattern as ilgi görmek, to get attention.

target: Bu restoranda çok lezzetli yemekler yapıyorlar.
english: They make very delicious food at this restaurant.
tip: yapıyorlar with no named subject means they in the general sense, like people make. It often reads as food is made here.

target: Marketten ekmek, süt ve peynir aldım.
english: I bought bread, milk, and cheese from the market.
tip: Market ends in a voiceless t, so the ablative from hardens to -ten, not -den: Marketten, from the market.

target: Onlar her zaman film izlerdi çünkü zamanları vardı.
english: They always watched movies because they had time.
tip: izlerdi is izle + r + di: used to watch. The -rdi ending marks a repeated past habit, not a single event.

english: He/She is not afraid of anything.
tip: korkmak pairs with ablative -den for what scares you: şeyden korkmaz means fears nothing, literally not afraid from anything.

english: Water boils at a hundred degrees.
tip: kaynar is kayna + r, the aorist -r for a general truth: water boils, always. The aorist states facts and habits, not one moment.
